title: Remediate Vite and Nx dependency advisories
objective: Update or constrain the vulnerable Vite and Nx dependency paths identified by pnpm audit, then validate the workspace and Architecture Studio without weakening audit policy.
validations: pnpm audit before: 17 advisories (6 high, 11 moderate) across vite (direct, apps/architecture-studio), axios and brace-expansion (both transitive via nx)
pnpm audit after: 'No known vulnerabilities found'

vite bumped 7.2.2 -> 7.3.6 (direct devDependency, apps/architecture-studio/package.json) -- patches all 5 Vite advisories (server.fs.deny bypass, arbitrary file read, Windows path bypass, optimized-deps .map path traversal, launch-editor NTLMv2)

axios and brace-expansion forced to ^1.18.1 / ^5.0.8 via pnpm-workspace.yaml's overrides field (not package.json's pnpm.overrides -- pnpm 11 no longer reads that location, confirmed by a real install warning, corrected before re-verifying) -- nx itself stays pinned at 23.1.0, still the latest stable release (23.2.0 has only beta/canary builds)
pnpm exec nx show projects: all 13 projects resolve correctly
pnpm --filter @grafting/architecture-studio build: real vite 7.3.6 production build succeeded (979 modules)
pnpm graph:generate: Graph IR candidate refreshed (this task's ownership/status change was itself the source of the staleness)
uv run --package automation python -m automation.coordination --root .: passed, 12 tasks
uv run --package automation python -m automation.control_plane --root .: passed, 0 model calls, 0 side effects, graph_candidate current
risks: pnpm's content-addressable store still holds the pre-override axios@1.16.1/brace-expansion@5.0.6 artifacts from before the override took effect in the correct location -- harmless (confirmed absent from pnpm-lock.yaml's actual resolved graph, which is what pnpm audit and the real dependency tree use), not cleaned up since store pruning is unrelated to this task's scope.

vite 7.2.2 -> 7.3.6 is a minor-version bump within the same major, not a full major upgrade -- low risk, verified by a real production build, but not exhaustively regression-tested beyond check+build.

Nx itself (23.1.0) was deliberately left on its current pinned version rather than bumped -- the transitive axios/brace-expansion advisories are patched via override instead, avoiding the unstable 23.2.0 beta/canary line the risk notes on this task already flagged as undesirable.
